claims.text: The solid-solution-annealed Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy has a single-phase FCC microstructure.
Local compositional fluctuations in Co-free FeNiCrMn produce spatially varying stacking-fault energies.
Moderate stacking-fault-energy variations promote dislocation cross-slip.
Moderate stacking-fault-energy variations stimulate localized short-range ordering.
Dislocation cross-slip and localized short-range ordering enhance strength in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Dislocation cross-slip and localized short-range ordering enhance ductility in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The proposed cross-slip and short-range-ordering synergy gives Co-free FeNiCrMn better dynamic performance than conventional Co-containing systems.
Inhomogeneous local ordering becomes more pronounced as temperature increases.
Inhomogeneous local ordering becomes more pronounced as strain rate increases.
Partial-dislocation motion becomes more pronounced as temperature or strain rate increases.
Dynamic slip and forest hardening stabilize plastic flow and delay fracture.
Co-free FeNiCrMn has greater strain-rate sensitivity than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi under comparable conditions.
At intermediate temperatures, Co-free FeNiCrMn has greater strain hardening than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
At intermediate temperatures, Co-free FeNiCrMn has greater ductility than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Co-free FeNiCrMn sustains more uniform deformation and absorbs more energy before failure than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Below about 77 K, above about 800 K, or outside strain rates of 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1, phase transformations, extensive dynamic recovery, or other deformation modes may supersede the proposed mechanism.
